exposure: Age (elderly primigravidae aged 35 years and above vs. young primigravidae aged 20-25 years)
Elderly primigravida (defined as a woman who goes into pregnancy for the first time at the age of 35 years or older)
cohort: 82 elderly primigravidae (study group) with a singleton gestation, compared to 131 young primigravidae (control group) who delivered at the same hospital from July 1st, 2005 to June 30th, 2010.
finding: Elderly primigravidae were significantly associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and operative obstetric interventions compared to younger primigravidae.
